overview: Andrew II of Hungary was a crusader king who led a royal expedition to the eastern Mediterranean during the Fifth Crusade.
His crusade shows how royal participation could serve prestige and vow-fulfillment even when military results were limited.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Andrew II of Hungary was a crusader king who led a royal expedition to the eastern Mediterranean during the Fifth Crusade.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Andrew came from the Árpád dynasty and ruled a kingdom marked by aristocratic privilege, royal grants, and regional ambitions in southeastern Europe.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Andrew II of Hungary is remembered as an ambitious but financially reckless king whose reign weakened the crown even as he pursued grand ventures abroad. The sources present a ruler of restless ambition who led the Fifth Crusade to the Holy Land — a campaign that achieved little — while at home his lavish grants of royal land and revenue to nobles and favourites depleted the monarchy and provoked a constitutional crisis.

That crisis produced the Golden Bull of 1222, a charter of noble liberties often compared to England's Magna Carta, which his own overspending and the resulting baronial pressure forced upon him. The chroniclers present a king more interested in prestige and generosity than in the careful husbanding of royal resources, whose open-handedness undermined the authority he sought to display.

What the record supports is an ambitious, prodigal, and ultimately weakening ruler, remembered as much for the concessions wrung from him as for his own initiatives. He is remembered as the crusading king whose financial improvidence and lavish grants forced the Golden Bull — a monarch whose ambitions abroad and generosity at home together eroded the strength of the Hungarian crown.

contentSections.title: As king and crusader
paragraphs: Andrew fulfilled a long-standing crusade vow by traveling east in 1217. His campaign in the Holy Land was brief and cautious, but it tied Hungarian kingship to crusading prestige.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Andrew died in 1235 after a reign better remembered in Hungary for the Golden Bull of 1222 than for eastern victories.
